input.summary: The paper claims 99.99% availability for a LEO optical-link terminal. No hardware, orbital trace, or full paper text is available. This draft identifies the key missing inputs (link-budget parameters, pass geometry, atmospheric model, and availability definition) and proposes a simulation-based independent check once those are resolved. Protocol is null pending three owner clarifications.
clarification_questions: What is the precise operational definition of 'availability' used in the paper — is it fraction of total LEO pass time with link margin above threshold, fraction of passes with at least one successful contact, or another metric, and what link-margin threshold (dB) applies?

Which atmospheric/weather impairment model and orbital parameters (altitude km, inclination °, ground-station latitude/longitude, minimum elevation angle °) does the paper use to derive the 99.99% figure?

Is a simulation tool, link-budget spreadsheet, or orbital-propagation script (e.g., STK, MATLAB, or open-source equivalent) referenced or available that could be used for an independent check, and if so, what version and configuration file hashes can be supplied?

proposal.problem: A LEO optical-link terminal is claimed to achieve 99.99% availability over LEO passes, but no hardware, orbital trace, atmospheric model, or full paper text is available to verify or reproduce this figure.
proposal.question: Under what orbital geometry, atmospheric impairment model, and link-budget assumptions does the proposed optical-link terminal achieve 99.99% availability over LEO passes, and can those assumptions be independently reproduced?
proposal.hypothesis: The proposed optical-link terminal maintains 99.99 percent availability over LEO passes.
proposal.conditions: Conditions are unresolved: orbital altitude, inclination, ground-station location, minimum elevation angle, link-margin threshold, and atmospheric/cloud-cover model are all unknown from the supplied metadata alone.
proposal.related_work: LEO optical-link availability analyses typically rely on orbital propagation (e.g., SGP4), atmospheric attenuation models (e.g., ITU-R P.1621), and cloud-cover statistics. No specific cited prior work is available from the supplied metadata.
proposal.alternatives: Alternative explanations for a 99.99% figure include: (a) availability defined over a single favorable ground station with low cloud cover; (b) diversity combining across multiple ground stations; (c) a narrow definition of 'pass' that excludes low-elevation contacts; or (d) an optimistic atmospheric model. These remain untested hypotheses.
proposal.design: An independent-check simulation would re-run the paper's orbital and link-budget model with identical parameters, then vary key assumptions (cloud cover, elevation mask, link margin) to assess sensitivity. Without the paper's model inputs, only a structural audit of the claim is possible at this stage.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: fraction of LEO pass time (or fraction of passes) with received optical power above the stated link-margin threshold, expressed as a percentage. Secondary metric: sensitivity of availability to ±5 dB link-margin variation and ±10° elevation-mask variation.
proposal.controls: Baseline control: availability computed under clear-sky, zero-loss conditions (upper bound). Negative control: availability under median global cloud-cover statistics (lower bound). Both controls bracket the claimed 99.99% figure.
proposal.falsification: The claim is falsified if an independent simulation using the paper's stated parameters yields availability below 99.99% under the paper's own atmospheric and orbital assumptions. It is also falsified if the 99.99% figure is only achievable under conditions not disclosed in the paper (e.g., multi-site diversity not mentioned in the claim).
proposal.inputs: Required but missing: (1) orbital parameters (altitude, inclination, RAAN); (2) ground-station coordinates and minimum elevation angle; (3) link-budget parameters (transmit power, aperture, wavelength, pointing loss, detector sensitivity); (4) atmospheric/cloud model and geographic scope; (5) availability definition and threshold. Source SHA-256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.
proposal.limitations: No hardware access, no orbital trace, and no full paper text are available. The source is retrieved-unreviewed synthetic metadata only. Any simulation would be an independent check of the paper's model, not a real-world measurement. Results cannot establish causality or generalize beyond the simulated scenario.
